messages:
carmen: heads-up: after installing the new windows msi (0.14.1) on my laptop, `redwoodctl login` immediately picks up an expired token from `%APPDATA%\\Redwood\\tokens.json` and fails with `invalid_grant`. fresh login via browser doesn't replace it.
dave: yikes. do you have both machine-wide and user installs on that device? we had a bug where the installer writes machine tokens to the per-user path on upgrade.
carmen: only user install. i inspected `%APPDATA%\\Redwood\\tokens.json` and it has a `last_refresh` timestamp from 2024-11-02. `redwoodctl auth list` shows the same token id under `default`.
infra-bot: detected matching issue: infra#4292 "windows: installer writes stale token to user data on upgrade" (opened 2026-02-09).
sophia: workaround: move the tokens file aside and run `redwoodctl login --web`. that will create a new token in the expected format. also `redwoodctl token revoke <id>` will clear server-side but CLI still reads local cache.
carmen: moving the file worked for me. but noticed another UX quirk: `redwoodctl whoami` after fresh login still prints `anonymous` until I `redwoodctl profile set current=work`. seems the installer didn't restore the previous profile pointer.
dave: that's two issues colliding. installer should not write tokens if migration fails, and we should prefer an env var > current pointer > token file ordering.
sophia: for a short-term patch: (1) change installer to write into `%APPDATA%\\Redwood\\tokens.json.tmp` and atomically replace only after validation, (2) add a CLI startup check: if token unreadable/expired, prompt `Found stale tokens at %APPDATA% - move them? [y/N]` instead of silently failing.
carmen: yes please. i hit this onboarding friction with a new hire earlier today and it took 30m to debug.
dave: i'll send a small PR updating the installer behavior and the CLI diagnostic: github.com/redwood-inference/redwoodctl/pull/6012 "windows: safe-write tokens + friendly stale-token diagnostic". also adding a `redwoodctl doctor` check that reports divergent profile pointers.
sophia: can we also add telemetry event when CLI falls back to local tokens so we can triage incidence rates? keep it opt-out.
support-bot: created support ticket #8420 for Carmen. suggested steps: move tokens file, run `redwoodctl login --web`, then `redwoodctl profile list` to confirm profile.
carmen: thanks all. after the workaround i'm unblocked and onboarding flow is back to normal. :white_check_mark:
